match.reason: The closest bank point, Embedded clauses, covers only adjectival clauses that add detail to a noun, while the new point also teaches adverbial clauses (when, where, why, how) and how fronting them changes emphasis, so it is broader and no bank point fits.

draft.title: Adjectival and adverbial clauses
card: a subordinate clause that adds detail to a noun. It often starts with who, which or that. In "The dog that barked all night is ours", the clause describes the dog.
a subordinate clause that tells when, where, why or how something happens. In "We ran inside because the rain began", the clause tells why we ran.
An adjectival clause sits right after the noun it describes. An adverbial clause adds detail to the action, and it often starts with a word such as when, because, after or where.

An adverbial clause can move to the front of a sentence. "When the bell rang, we left" puts the time first, so it is stressed more than in "We left when the bell rang". A comma follows the clause at the front.
draft.remember: Adjectival clauses describe a noun. Adverbial clauses tell when, where, why or how, and can move to the front for emphasis.

a.q: In "Mia met the girl who won the race", what does the clause "who won the race" do?
opts: It adds detail to the noun girl
It tells when Mia met the girl
It tells why Mia met the girl
It adds detail to the verb met
a.why: The clause starts with who and describes the girl, so it is adjectival. It does not tell when, why or how Mia met her, which is what an adverbial clause would do.
a.clue: Ask which noun the clause tells you more about.

b.q: Which sentence has an adverbial clause at the front, so the reason is stressed?
opts: Because the creek flooded, we stayed home
We stayed home because the creek flooded
The creek that flooded was behind our house
We stayed in the house that Dad built
b.why: "Because the creek flooded" is an adverbial clause of reason, placed first. The second option has the same clause at the end, so it is not at the front. The last two options have clauses starting with that, which are adjectival.
b.clue: Look for a reason clause that comes before the main part.

a.best: It adds detail to the noun girl

b.best: Because the creek flooded, we stayed home

problems.detail: The why says the reason is 'not stressed' when the clause comes at the end, but the card only says fronting stresses it 'more'. End position also carries emphasis (end focus), so the why should say the reason is stressed less, not that it is not stressed.
